dedupe_keys.name: construction spending value of construction put in place survey vip

description: The Value of Construction Put in Place Survey (VIP) of the U.S. Census Bureau provides monthly estimates of the total dollar value of construction work done in the United States, on new structures and improvements to existing structures, for the private and public sectors. Spending is published by type of construction, including power (power plants of all fuels, hydroelectric, wind and solar facilities, transmission and distribution), highway and street, sewage and waste disposal, water supply (plants, transmission lines, culverts, tunnels), conservation and development (dams, levees, locks), transportation (air, land and water facilities), communication, and residential, commercial, educational and health care buildings. Coverage: national monthly series with annual totals, public spending split by state and local and federal ownership; an experimental monthly series gives Census division estimates for private manufacturing construction. Access: monthly release tables and historical time series on the web page, the Census Data API economic indicators time series (timeseries/eits), and FRED; free and public domain. Caveats: national aggregates in current dollars; maintenance and repairs are excluded, and the page notes that natural disasters can affect the compilation. Simulation uses: trends in investment by infrastructure type for capacity expansion and renewal scenarios, cost indices for replacement and recovery estimates, and context for asset ageing models. Related records: the Building Permits Survey, New Residential Construction, State and Local Government Finances (capital outlay by function) and the ASCE Infrastructure Report Card.
